Influenza Outbreak Disrupts Canadian Banking Operations

A significant influenza outbreak is disrupting operations across Canada’s banking industry, with multiple institutions reporting staff shortages and temporary branch closures. The flu strain, identified by health officials last week, has rapidly spread among employees at urban and regional banking sites, leading to mounting absenteeism.

According to the Canadian Banking Employers Council, nearly 15% of the industry’s workforce is currently on sick leave. “We are seeing unprecedented levels of staff illness, particularly in Ontario and British Columbia,” said Council spokesperson James Renaud. “Banks are responding by reducing branch hours and consolidating services at key locations to maintain essential operations.”

Firms have implemented enhanced sanitation procedures and shifted more customer service functions to digital platforms, yet the outbreak continues to strain day-to-day activities. At First Dominion Bank, more than 40 branches have temporarily closed, while others are operating with skeleton crews. “Our priority is the health and safety of our employees and customers,” said Sandra Ho, the firm’s chief operating officer. “We’re encouraging remote work wherever possible and redeploying teams to cover critical functions.”

Employee unions are raising concerns about burnout among remaining staff. “Those who are still able to work are under tremendous pressure,” said Melissa Tran, representative of the Canadian Bank Workers’ Union. “We urge banks to provide additional support and flexible arrangements during this period.”

Analysts note that the outbreak’s duration remains uncertain. “The longer the situation persists, the more challenging it becomes to maintain service quality and operational resilience,” observed Martin Gauthier, industry analyst at Northstar Research. No timeline has yet been provided for a return to normal operations, as firms continue to monitor the evolving situation closely.
